review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped related files for pderiv lemmas and any @[simp] annotations in the Torus directory (none found). The file has no simp attributes. The two findings are modest interface gaps: missing projection simp lemmas for the `bData` def, and the unconditional `pderiv_neg` used only by manual rw plus `simp only` beta-reduction. I did not find a loop or competing rules. `Util_symm` is correctly not a simp lemma because it is a symmetric swap. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas are untested.

findings.excerpt: def bData (n : ℕ) (u₀ : (Fin n → ℝ) → (Fin N → ℝ))
findings.problem: `bData` is a plain def building a `GuntherData` structure, with no projection simp lemmas such as `(bData n u₀ h).a i = vcoeff n (dualA u₀ i)`, and likewise for `.b` and `.h`. Every downstream use must either close the goal by definitional unfolding (`:= rfl` at line 211, bare `rfl` at lines 519, 528, 537) or run `simp only [bData]`, which unfolds the whole structure (line 257). This is brittle, and it makes the simp-normal form of `(bData …).h p q` depend on unfolding the definition.
findings.proposed_change: Add three `@[simp]` projection lemmas, e.g. `bData_a`, `bData_b`, `bData_h`, each with proof `rfl`. For example, `(bData n u₀ h).h p q = stdFourierCoeff n (fun x => ((h x p q : ℝ) : ℂ))`. Then replace `hh2 := rfl`, the `simp only [bData]` and the trailing `rfl`s with `simp only [bData_h, bData_b]` or `rw`, and keep `bData` itself opaque to simp.
findings.benefit: Gives a canonical normal form for the data projections and removes ad hoc defeq closers. Proofs about `gC`/`gB` of `bData` rewrite to the Fourier-coefficient expressions without unfolding the whole structure.

findings.excerpt:
lemma pderiv_neg (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) (i : Fin n) :
    pderiv i (fun y => -f y) = fun y => -pderiv i f y := by
findings.problem: This is an unconditional, directional (differentiation of a negation pushed inward) identity. Its docstring says 'for smooth scalar f', but it has no smoothness hypothesis, unlike its siblings `pderiv_add` and `pderiv_sub`. It is not tagged simp and is stated only in eta-expanded lambda form. As a result it is applied by hand with `rw [hfun_j, pderiv_neg (Ftil n v j)] at hpr_i`, followed by a bare `simp only at hpr_i hpr_j` just to beta-reduce. A reader cannot tell whether it is part of the simp set.
findings.proposed_change: Fix the docstring (no smoothness needed). Optionally state it in the unapplied form `pderiv i (-f) = -pderiv i f`, plus a pointwise `pderiv i (fun y => -f y) x = -pderiv i f x`, and mark these `@[simp]`, since the right side is structurally smaller and cannot loop. Then lines 824–826 become a single `simp` or `rw` without the extra beta-reduction step.
findings.benefit: Removes the manual rw/beta-reduce dance and gives `pderiv` a canonical negation rule that is findable and consistent in orientation. It also makes the missing-hypothesis situation explicit for users of the sibling lemmas.

evidence.excerpt: rw [hfun_j, pderiv_neg (Ftil n v j)] at hpr_i
/-- `∂ᵢ` of a sum of smooth maps. -/
